advances: Absolute two-source cap bounds for dilates of a single centered convex body at a specified mark. The supplied array has only the two endpoint sources, and a total-mass normalized bound for arbitrary bodies is outside this setting.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Write $p_{(A,B)}(0)$ for the raw depth of the array at $(0,0)$. Tighten any containing halfspace parallel to its boundary until it passes through $(0,0)$. When the continuous normal is $u\ne0$, its margin is $tz+u\cdot x$ and the thresholds at the two bases are $t,-t$. The captured volume from $(rK,sK)$ is then $V[r^dF_u(t/r)+s^dF_u(-t/s)]$. Every such $u,t$ is realized by a through-point halfspace. A through-point halfspace with purely base normal captures one entire source, of volume at least $r^dV$.

**Equal scales.** For $(K,K)$ apply 6a7d56e450b3126f to the uniform law on $K$, with centroid zero and shift $|t|$. Every nonzero continuous normal gives mass at least $2\Gamma_d V$. The pure-base mass $V$ is also at least $2\Gamma_d V$, since the binomial expansion gives $(1+1/d)^d\ge2$, strictly for $d\ge2$. Thus $p_{(K,K)}(0)\ge2\Gamma_d V$. This also gives the equal-scale bound directly by scaling.

**Exact large-ratio range.** For $u\ne0$ let $[-a,b]$ be the support interval of $u\cdot K$. The mean estimate proved in 0255a3c283c1a796 gives a distance from the mean to either support endpoint of at most $d(a+b)/(d+1)$. It applies with $K$ as the sole integer fiber of $[-1/2,1/2]\times K$ and the mean equal to zero. Therefore $a\le db$ and $b\le da$ in every direction, giving $-K\subseteq dK$ by support functions. Since $0\in K$, if $s\ge dr$ then $sK\supseteq-rK$. For every $u\ne0$ and real $t$ the two caps then have combined mass at least
$$
|rK\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge t\}|+|(-rK)\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge-t\}|=r^dV.
$$
Reflection makes the second cap the closed complement in $rK$ up to the common hyperplane, which has zero $d$-volume. For fixed $u$, the scalar cost is continuous by nullity of hyperplanes and constant on either side of a compact interval, so a minimum exists. For any $r\le s$, choosing $t\le\min\{r\min_K u\cdot x,-s\max_K u\cdot x\}$ makes the smaller cap full and the larger cap empty or a null supporting face, so the scalar cost equals $r^d$ at that finite threshold. For $s\ge dr$ this achieves the minimum, and a pure-base halfspace capturing just $rK$ gives the matching upper bound for array depth. In dimension one the centered interval has $-K=K$ and $dr=r$, so this covers the whole range.

**Interpolation.** Let $d\ge2$ and $r\le s\le dr$. Set
$$
\alpha=\frac{dr-s}{d-1},\qquad \beta=\frac{s-r}{d-1}.
$$
These coefficients are nonnegative, with $\alpha+\beta=r>0$ and $\alpha+d\beta=s$. Convexity of $K$ gives the componentwise identity $(rK,sK)=\alpha(K,K)+\beta(K,dK)$, omitting any term with zero coefficient. The arrays have the same affinely independent bases $-1,1$ in $\mathbb R$, with barycentric weights $1/2,1/2$ and base mark zero. Their components are full-dimensional compact convex bodies, and the continuous mark zero belongs to each weighted Minkowski section because $0\in K$. The homogeneous pointwise inequality in 4fc403cf46f23e49 at these marks gives
$$
p_{(rK,sK)}(0)^{1/d}
\ge V^{1/d}(\alpha c_d+\beta)
=V^{1/d}\left[r c_d+\frac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right].
$$
This controls the mass of every through-point halfspace, hence every scalar cost. At $s=r$ the bracket is $r c_d$ and at $s=dr$ it is $r$. The homogeneous theorem includes the one-coefficient-zero cases. For $d\ge2$ we have $c_d<1$, so the bracket strictly exceeds $r c_d$ when $s>r$ in this range, and the exact large-ratio value $r^d$ also exceeds $2\Gamma_d r^d$. The interpolation provides a lower bound in the open range $r<s<dr$.
statement:
Let $d\ge1$, and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body of volume $V>0$ and volume centroid zero. Let $0<r\le s$, and for $u\ne0$ define $F_u(t)=|K\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge t\}|/V$, where $|\cdot|$ is $d$-dimensional volume.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}$. Define
$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r, & d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d, & d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d, & d\ge2,\ s\ge dr.
\end{cases}
$$
The two $d\ge2$ branches agree at $s=dr$.

For every $u\ne0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$
r^dF_u(t/r)+s^dF_u(-t/s)\ge\Phi_d(r,s).
$$
If $d\ge2$ and $s>r$, then $\Phi_d(r,s)>2\Gamma_d r^d$. For each fixed $u\ne0$ the minimum of the left side over $t\in\mathbb R$ is at most $r^d$. It equals $r^d$ and is attained at a finite threshold if $s\ge dr$, which includes every $0<r\le s$ in dimension one.

For the supplied array with just $rK$ at base $-1$ and $sK$ at base $1$, the raw source depth at $(0,0)$ is at least $V\Phi_d(r,s)$, and is exactly $Vr^d$ if $s\ge dr$. Here raw source depth is the infimum, over closed ambient halfspaces containing $(0,0)$, of the sum of the volumes captured from the two supplied sources.
title: Paired cap bounds for unequal homothetic sources
